primary_cause: Mall-REIT stress tied to closures tenant bankruptcies and rent-collection uncertainty with Simon reopening only 49 malls starting May 1-2
secondary_factors: Reopening execution risk exposure to weaker apparel tenants and broad reopening trade skepticism
store_description: Investors were discounting SPG for a severe cash-flow shock with Simon later disclosing $8.7B liquidity but the market far more worried about unpaid rent and whether shoppers would return.

primary_cause: COVID demand shock telegraphed by Starbucks Apr 8 preliminary warning of fiscal Q2 EPS around $0.28 down from $0.53 a year earlier
secondary_factors: Store-closure uncertainty weak mobility data and concern reopening would be gradual rather than V-shaped
store_description: Starbucks told investors U.S. comps began falling March 12 and worsened through quarter-end with over 2000 China stores closed earlier in the quarter.

primary_cause: Continued repricing of rate-sensitive brokerage earnings under ultra-low rates with no fresh Apr 28-30 event found
secondary_factors: Banking-sector weakness recession fears and concern zero rates would squeeze client-cash economics
store_description: Schwab was caught in the earnings-model problem hitting financials broadly with near-zero rates compressing spread income even when client activity was strong.

primary_cause: Southern Q1 on Apr 30 showed GAAP EPS falling to $0.82 from $2.01 a year earlier driven by absence of prior-year asset-sale gains
secondary_factors: General utility de-risking and worries about financing heavy capex programs such as Vogtle
store_description: Southern's reported earnings of $868M or $0.82/share versus $2.08B or $2.01/share a year earlier drove the decline even though adjusted EPS actually rose to $0.78 from $0.70.

primary_cause: Ongoing repricing of bank credit risk and capital-markets cyclicality with no clean fresh Apr 28-May 1 headline found
secondary_factors: Recession fears credit-loss provisioning across banks and continued skepticism toward financials
store_description: Goldman's Apr 15 earnings with EPS of $3.11 and sharply higher credit provisions remained the dominant overhang with no new catalyst verified.

primary_cause: Elon Musk tweeted Tesla stock price is too high imo on May 1 causing Reuters to report about 9% decline erasing roughly $13 billion in market value
secondary_factors: Musk's same-day stream of erratic tweets and fresh concern over SEC/communications risk
store_description: One of the cleanest names on the list with Tesla hit immediately and directly after Musk's tweet.

primary_cause: Texas Instruments Apr 21 Q1 results guided Q2 revenue to $2.94B-$3.46B and EPS to $0.78-$1.08 signaling major demand uncertainty
secondary_factors: Cyclicality in industrial analog chips and macro fears about factory shutdowns
store_description: TI's Q1 print was decent but the market cared more about the soft Q2 framework and management's caution on auto and industrial end-market visibility.

primary_cause: Collapse in ride-hailing demand with rides down 60-70% in some cities and withdrawn 2020 outlook plus $1.9-2.2B expected write-downs
secondary_factors: Uncertainty around profitability and fear that Eats growth would not fully offset Mobility
store_description: Uber was still trading as a collapse-in-mobility story with the decline reflecting continued concern after pulled forecasts and material write-downs.

primary_cause: Regional-bank credit-loss and zero-rate pressure with no decisive fresh USB-only headline found and U.S. bank profits down 69.6% YoY
secondary_factors: Consumer credit exposure recession expectations and broad financial-sector weakness
store_description: USB looked more like a bank-complex move than a unique single-name event with continued repricing of loan-loss risk in near-zero-rate environment.

primary_cause: Ongoing concern about Wells Fargo's earnings power reserve needs and regulatory overhang including the still-active Fed asset cap
secondary_factors: Dividend-cut fears low-rate pressure and general bank selloff
store_description: WFC was one of the weakest large-bank stories combining recession-driven credit losses with an already constrained franchise under regulatory restrictions.

primary_cause: Exxon reported on May 1 its first quarterly loss in 30 years at $610 million including a $2.9 billion charge from inventory valuation and impairments
secondary_factors: Capex cuts collapsing fuel demand and concern even Exxon's balance sheet would be strained
store_description: Exxon posted a $610M loss versus $2.4B profit a year earlier confirming the COVID oil shock had overwhelmed even the strongest integrated majors.

primary_cause: Commercial aerospace collapse overwhelming the otherwise stronger defense business with no Apr 28-May 1 RTX earnings release
secondary_factors: Uncertainty around the Raytheon/UTC integration and airline aftermarket demand
store_description: Investors viewed the defense franchise as supportive but not enough to offset the commercial-aero shock with full disclosure not arriving until May 7.

primary_cause: Ongoing shutdown/cash-burn fears with GM having drawn $16B from credit lines and suspended guidance after plant shutdowns
secondary_factors: Uncertainty over restart timing with North American plants not restarting until May 18 and demand destruction
store_description: GM did not need a fresh headline with the core issue being survival math after roughly two months of lost production and ongoing cash burn.

primary_cause: Expected demand destruction in farm and heavy equipment ahead of the May 22 earnings that later showed profit down 41%
secondary_factors: Industrial/cyclical selloff and fear that dealer inventories and customer financing would come under pressure
store_description: No major Deere-specific release found with the move reflecting forward discounting of cyclical earnings deterioration later confirmed.

primary_cause: GE Q1 on Apr 29 showed COVID especially painful in Aviation with industrial free cash flow at negative $2.2B and adjusted EPS of $0.05 vs $0.08 expected
secondary_factors: Power losses and fear the balance-sheet repair story would be delayed again
store_description: GE explicitly said commercial aerospace deteriorated sharply in March with aviation profit falling 39% to $1.0B while targeting $2B+ cost cuts and $3B cash preservation.

primary_cause: Applied Materials fiscal Q2 on Apr 28 showed revenue $3.96B vs consensus ~$4.13B and non-GAAP EPS $0.89 vs ~$0.94 expected
secondary_factors: Concern about customer capex delays and weak near-term memory/foundry visibility
store_description: Applied missed on both revenue and adjusted EPS which hurt a cyclical equipment name in an already fragile tape.

primary_cause: Post-earnings giveback despite strong Q1 with revenue up 40% to $1.79B and gross margin expanding to 46%
secondary_factors: Semiconductor-sector weakness and concern consumer/enterprise spending could soften later in the year
store_description: AMD's numbers were strong so the decline looks like a valuation reset move rather than a bad-news drop with the market wanting more aggressive guidance.

primary_cause: Mild post-earnings sell-the-news reaction after Apr 30 beat with GAAP EPS falling 3% to $3.07 from higher costs and Otezla amortization
secondary_factors: Pandemic-related healthcare utilization uncertainty
store_description: Amgen's print was fine but not a blowout that forces a biotech higher in a risk-off tape with no dramatic guidance raise.

primary_cause: Amazon Apr 30 warned Q2 operating income could range from $1.5B profit to $1.5B loss as it expected to spend $4 billion on COVID measures
secondary_factors: Margin compression in e-commerce supply-chain disruption and disappointment revenue strength would not flow to profit
store_description: Amazon's quarter was strong on demand but the market focused on the $4B COVID spending warning turning a pandemic winner into a near-term margin story.

primary_cause: Supplier/consumer-electronics demand worries especially through Apple exposure rather than a fresh Broadcom-only shock
secondary_factors: Tech hardware cyclicality and general de-risking in semis on global demand uncertainty
store_description: No major Broadcom-specific release found with the decline reflecting customer-exposure contagion from weak iPhone demand and disrupted supply chains.
